title: Fibre-generating sections define a proper projective-space morphism near the fibre
statement: Let $f:Z\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $s\in S$, and let $Z_s$ be its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $r\geq0$, and let $u_0,\ldots,u_r\in\Gamma(Z,M)$. Assume their pullbacks to $Z_s$ [def-pc-module-pullback] generate $M_s=M|_{Z_s}$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. There is an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the restricted $u_j$ generate $M_U=M|_{Z_U}$ on $Z_U=f^{-1}(U)$. Their associated $U$-morphism $\varphi:Z_U\to\mathbf P^r_U$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is proper and has a quotient-compatible isomorphism $\varphi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong M_U$. Its base change to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is the morphism $Z_s\to\mathbf P^r_{\kappa(s)}$ associated to the pulled-back tuple, with the same quotient-compatible twist isomorphism. Projective space is [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]; over the affine $U$ its twist is [def-pc-projective-space-twist].

source.place: Tag 0D2N, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, first paragraph from the nonvanishing opens through construction of phi and identification of its fibre.

proof.text: Pullback preserves invertibility, so $M_s$ is invertible. For each $j$ put $W_j=Z_{u_j}$, the locus where $u_j$ has nonzero residue value, and put $W=\bigcup_{j=0}^rW_j$. The nonvanishing-section lemma makes each $W_j$ open. Let $i_s:Z_s\to Z$ be the fibre projection. Nonvanishing commutes with pullback, so the nonvanishing locus of $i_s^*u_j$ is $i_s^{-1}(W_j)$. Apply the generating-sections fibre criterion on $Z_s$: the hypothesis implies $Z_s=\bigcup_j i_s^{-1}(W_j)$. The fibre projection identifies $|Z_s|$ with $f^{-1}(s)$, hence $f^{-1}(s)\subseteq W$.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood: the opens X_{s_i} cover the fibre; Modules Tag 01CY, lemma-s-open and remark-pullback-s-open

proof.text: Put $C=|Z|\setminus W$. It is closed. Properness includes universal closedness, so $f(C)$ is closed (use the identity base change). No point of $C$ maps to $s$, by step 1. Thus $V=S\setminus f(C)$ is an open neighbourhood of $s$ and $f^{-1}(V)\subseteq W$. Choose an affine open $s\in U\subseteq V$ using the affine-opens basis. The restriction $M_U$ is invertible by pullback stability. Nonvanishing commutes with the open pullback $Z_U\to Z$, so the nonvanishing opens of $u_j|_{Z_U}$ cover $Z_U$. The generating-sections criterion now gives generation of $M_U$ by that restricted tuple.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood: since X to Y is closed shrink so f^{-1}(V) is in the union; Schemes Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens

proof.text: Apply the projective-space functor of points to $(M_U,(u_j|_{Z_U}))$, obtaining $\psi:Z_U\to\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\alpha:\psi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z}}(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}M_U$ sending every pulled-back $T_j$ to $u_j|_{Z_U}$. The definition of the morphism by sections gives $\varphi=(f_U,\psi):Z_U\to U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z}$, a $U$-morphism. Write $\rho$ for the second projection. The standard-chart lemma defines the relative twist as $\rho^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z}}(1)$. Since $\rho\varphi=\psi$, the composite-pullback isomorphism identifies $\varphi^*\mathcal O(1)$ with $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)$; compose with $\alpha$. This carries $\varphi^*T_j$ to $u_j|_{Z_U}$ and is therefore quotient-compatible. Over $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ the chart rings are $A[T_l/T_j:l\ne j]$, with overlap maps given by the same fractions. By the polynomial-Proj chart lemma these are precisely the charts $D_+(x_j)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A[x_l/x_j:l\ne j]$ of $\operatorname{Proj}(A[x_0,\ldots,x_r])$, with $D_+(x_i)\cap D_+(x_j)$ the basic open of $x_i/x_j$ in $D_+(x_j)$ and with twist bases satisfying $e_i=(x_i/x_j)e_j$; their coordinate-preserving identifications ($T_l/T_j\mapsto x_l/x_j$) therefore agree on overlaps and glue. The twist frames $T_j$ satisfy $T_i=(T_i/T_j)T_j$, exactly the transition rule of the specified affine twist, so the twist identification also glues.

source.place: Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space; definition-projective-space and its following paragraph; Tag 01NG, lemma-standard-covering-projective-space

proof.text: The restriction $f_U:Z_U\to U$ is a base change of $f$, hence proper. The structural map $q:\mathbf P^r_U\to U$ is proper by the projective-space properness lemma with finite coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,r\}$; in particular it is separated by the definition of properness. We have $q\varphi=f_U$ by step 3. Apply proper-over-separated cancellation to this triangle to conclude that $\varphi$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 01W4, lemma-base-change-proper; Tag 01W6, lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed (2); Constructions Tag 01NH, lemma-projective-space-separated

proof.text: Let $b:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to U$ and $i:Z_s\to Z_U$ be the fibre maps. The universal property of fibre products identifies $(U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z})\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z}$, preserving both projections: in either case a map into it is a pair of maps to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z}$ with equal composites to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The second projection of $\varphi_s$ is $\psi i$. Naturality in the functor-of-points lemma identifies $\psi i$ with the morphism classified by $(i^*M_U,(i^*u_j))$. Its first projection is the fibre structure map, so uniqueness in the fibre-product definition proves that $\varphi_s$ is the associated morphism over $\kappa(s)$. Pull back the isomorphism of step 3 along $i$ and use composite pullback: it sends each pulled-back coordinate $T_j$ to $i^*u_j$. This is precisely the same quotient-compatible twist isomorphism on the fibre. Indeed on the nonvanishing opens, which cover by the fibre hypothesis, such an isomorphism must send the coordinate generator to the specified generator, so it is unique.
